title: I Let the Ice-Resurfacer Log Catch the Coach Who Skipped Our Flood

parts.text: I stepped into sheet one at 9:07 p.m. and coach Britt was already using our numbered flood. The board said: ONE FLOOD. TWELVE MINUTES. ICE STAYS WITH THE BOOKING. I was thirty-four, rink steward, holding a clipboard that listed our resurface. Britt shrugged. "Coaches keep the ice." I photographed the board, the booking, and her skaters on our wet ice. Then I asked for the resurfacer log. At 9:11 the rink desk pinged why Britt's skaters sat on our flood. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The rink desk can see Britt's skaters on sheet one during our flood.

social.video_title: She skipped our numbered ice flood — Part 1/2
social.description: Ice rink, a coach on our flood, a twelve-minute clock she posted. I logged the skaters. Would you have asked for the resurfacer log?

parts.text: Britt called it cool-down laps until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the flood still. The flood went back to our numbered window. Britt ran a slot of their own and told the next coach atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: COACHES DO NOT KEEP THE ICE. I keep our resurface on a labeled card. Britt brown-bags her laps. The sheet finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Coaches do not keep the ice — Part 2/2
social.description: Resurfacer log, numbered flood, and a second line on the board. Were cool-down laps ever our flood?
